subject: Highwater renewal & capacity anchoring
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@highwater.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion + capacity uplift request

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick onboarding support last quarter. Highwater has seen sustained growth for our real-time assistant pipelines; our usage is currently trending 2.4x above the commit we signed in Jan. We want to lock a renewal now (12 months) and increase committed capacity ~2x to avoid mid-quarter price surprises.

Key asks from our side:
- A limited price hold for the first 6-9 months while we optimize prompts and move to KV caching.
- One-time operational credit to cover the ramp month where we expect 40% overage.
- Clear burst capacity guarantee for Black Friday (we need predictable access to double capacity for up to 48 hours).

Can Redwood propose options that balance our desire for a short-term price protection with a pathway to a higher commit? Procurement (copied in a follow-up) will need a clear SOW and a redline-friendly amendment.

I attached a usage snapshot for June and projected July numbers. Happy to hop on a 30m call next week.

Regards,
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Product Operations
Highwater
Attachment: Highwater_usage_snapshot_Jun2027.csv (CSV, 78KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@highwater.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + capacity uplift request

Aisha —

Thanks for the details and the snapshot — helpful. Congrats on the growth. We've pulled the utilization data and sketched three options that aim to give you runway while protecting Redwood's operating economics: 

1) Conservative onramp (12m): 1.25x commit, no up-front discount, 30% one-time ramp credit to offset initial overages, standard burst access (best-effort).
2) Anchored renewal (12m): 2x commit, 9-month price hold on current base rate, one-time capacity credit (150k tokens) applied to first invoice, guaranteed burst pool of +1.5x for scheduled events (72h notice).
3) Partnership ladder (24m): 2.5x commit, 18% tiered discount, larger operational credits, and a committed burst SLA for up to 96 hours per event.

To evaluate: we need a 3-month rolling forecast and a primary procurement contact so Legal can prep an amendment. David — can you confirm whether the burst SLA in option 2 is something we can commit to operationally (load testing / reserved capacity)?

I've attached a draft term sheet for option 2 (fast path). If that looks good to you, we can generate an SOW annex and a DocuSign package. Proposed next steps: 30m call Mon or Tue; signature target Aug 15 to align billing cycles.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Highwater_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:17:00 -07:00

Evelyn / David —

Appreciate the options. A few clarifications from procurement/ops: 
- We prefer the Anchored renewal but would ask for a 9-month price hold (instead of 6) and a staged credit release: 50% on sign, 50% after month 3 if usage normalizes.
- Burst SLA: we need a documented change-control process for guaranteed reserved capacity (scheduled events only).
- Can you include a short note on data handling for logs during burst windows (we have internal compliance to address)?

Procurement lead: Rahul Desai (rahul.desai@highwater.com) — I'll loop in our legal once we have a redline.

Thanks,
Rahul Desai
Director, Procurement & Vendor Ops

Eve — quick internal: ops sanity check passed for option 2. We can commit to a scheduled reserved burst pool (requires 72h schedule and small pre-reservation fee) and can carve the 150k token credit out of the first invoice. Monica, can Legal carve a 9-month price hold clause and staged credit release into the amendment? If Procurement wants a staged 50/50 release, we should tie second tranche to usage falling below 1.6x commit for months 2-3.

-David

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Highwater renewal — updated proposal + DocuSign

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment we can move forward on the Anchored renewal with the following negotiated bullets: 
- Term: 12 months starting on sign date.
- Commit: 2x current baseline.
- Price hold: 9 months at current base rate, then step to new tier thereafter (see attached schedule).
- One-time capacity credit: 150,000 tokens, released 50% at sign, 50% after month 3 conditional on normalized usage (<1.6x commit).
- Burst: scheduled reserved pool (1.5x) available with 72h notice; pre-reservation fee applies for sustained events >24h.
- Compliance: Redwood will provide a short annex describing log retention/handling during burst windows and confirm no added data residency changes.

I've attached the updated redline and SOW annex (HW-SOW-Annex.xlsx). If this matches your expectation, I've created a DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.fake/agree/HW-2027-042. Target signature date: Aug 15 to avoid mid-month billing churn.

Next steps: Rahul/procurement to review redline; if approved I'll route to Legal for final sign and then Ops to provision the reserved pool.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Highwater_Renewal_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 158KB), HW-SOW-Annex.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)
